subject: Audit logging & SOC 2 follow-up: notes and next steps
messages:

Subject: Audit logging & SOC 2 follow-up: notes and next steps

Hi Jordan / Devon -

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we're all aligned:

Recap (what we covered)
- Redwood status: SOC 2 program in flight (Type II audit scheduled; target report availability: Q3 2026). We currently maintain SOC 2 controls and have completed internal readiness reviews.
- Audit logging scope: admin activity logs, API request/response metadata, authentication events, and exportability to customer-managed sinks (S3/Blob, SIEM).
- Key questions raised: immutability guarantees, export formats, retention defaults, inclusion of prompt content in logs.

Capabilities (high-level)
- Admin activity logs: all console actions (role changes, permission updates, user provisioning) with actor, timestamp, and before/after where applicable.
- API logs: request_id, timestamp, endpoint, model variant, principal (API key or scoped service account), token counts, response status. By default we store metadata; full request bodies (prompts) are not stored unless customer enables full-request logging in dedicated/private deployments.
- Exportability: daily and real-time export options to S3, secure streaming to SIEM (Splunk/Datadog), and on-demand bulk export (GZIP/JSONL).
- Immutability: for hosted customers we provide signed digests and append-only store for the retention window; for Private customers we support WORM S3 object lock and signed manifests for long-term retention.

Attachments: I've attached our audit-logging overview and I included your questionnaire (ACME_Security_RQ_2026.pdf).

Next steps
1) Marissa: provide a short technical log schema and sample export (Logan will attach). Target ETA: 24 hours.
2) Acme: mark any high-priority questionnaire items; we'll start filling the vendor security questionnaire and return evidence links.
3) Tech deep-dive: Logan to schedule a 45-60min technical session to demo export and immutability options. Proposed times below.

Proposed meeting slots (PST):
- Tue 2026-07-14 10:00-11:00
- Wed 2026-07-15 14:00-15:00

Thanks - looking forward to next steps.

Best,

Hi Marissa - thanks for the recap, that's helpful. A few clarifying items from our security team so we can prioritize the questionnaire:

1) Immutability: can you confirm the immutability guarantee for hosted customers? Is it cryptographic append-only with signed digests, or do you rely on retention policies only? We need assurances for tamper-evidence during the retention window.
2) Prompt data: does Redwood log prompt text or model outputs by default in the hosted product? If not, what are our options to capture specific request bodies for compliance?
3) Encryption & key management: are logs encrypted at rest? Do customers have the option to use customer-managed keys (CMKs) or HSM-backed keys for exported archives?
4) Sample artifacts: can you share a sample log schema and a small (redacted) sample export so our SecOps can validate fields?

We'd like to start the vendor security questionnaire today - I attached ACME_Security_RQ_2026.pdf in my local copy; you can mark items you can respond to now and we'll route anything that needs legal/SLA review.

Also would like to lock a time for the tech deep-dive - Tue 10:00 PST works for me if Logan is available.

Thanks,
Jordan Smith
Head of Security Operations
Acme Corp
jordan.smith@acme.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 13 Jul 2026 11:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Audit logging & SOC 2 follow-up: notes and next steps

Jordan - great questions, answered inline below. I'll coordinate with Logan to get the samples over and lock the Tue slot if that works.

1) Immutability- Hosted customers: we provide tamper-evident append-only logs within the retention window and publish signed SHA256 manifests for exported bundles. For customers requiring stronger guarantees we recommend using Private deployment or exporting to a customer-managed S3 bucket with Object Lock (WORM).

2) Prompt data- By default hosted telemetry and API logs capture metadata and not full prompt text. We can enable full request logging for specific customers or routes (this is more common for Dedicated/Private deployments). When full-request logging is enabled we have controls to redact or mask sensitive fields.

3) Encryption & KMS- Logs are encrypted at rest. For hosted customers we manage KMS keys by default; for Dedicated and Private we support customer-managed keys (AWS KMS, GCP KMS) and HSM integrations for exported archives.

4) Sample artifacts- Logan will attach a sample schema and a redacted JSONL export. Expect fields for request_id, timestamp, principal_id, endpoint, model, tokens_in, tokens_out, status_code, latency_ms, and optional request_body (redacted).

Next actions:
- Logan: will send sample_log_schema.json and a 5-10 line sample export.
- Marissa: I'll start filling out the questionnaire and return a preliminary pass by EOD tomorrow.
- Jordan: confirm Tue 10:00 PST for the tech deep-dive.

Thanks - I'll be on the call with Logan.

Best,
Marissa

Retention and immutability notes
- Hosted: default retention 90 days, append-only internal store with signed manifests produced daily. Exportable bundles can be pulled and verified against signed digests.
- Dedicated/Private: configurable retention up to 7 years, support for S3 Object Lock (WORM), and ability to send directly to customer-managed buckets with CMKs and object-lock enabled.

Export formats
- JSONL (gzip) for bulk exports
- Streaming webhook/SIEM (RFC5424-like events) for real-time ingestion
- CSV summary bundles for quick audit review
